title: Saturated and unsaturated fatty acids
caption: All three are 18 carbons long with a –COOH head. Stearic acid has no double bonds and is straight; each cis double bond in oleic and linoleic acid puts a kink in the chain, so they pack loosely and their fats are liquid.
alt: Skeletal structures of stearic acid with no double bonds, oleic acid with one cis double bond and linoleic acid with two, each with 18 carbons.
description: Stearic acid, C₁₈H₃₆O₂: saturated, a straight chain.
Oleic acid, C₁₈H₃₄O₂: monounsaturated, one cis double bond and a kink.
Linoleic acid, C₁₈H₃₂O₂: polyunsaturated, two cis double bonds and two kinks.
Kinked chains cannot pack closely, so unsaturated fats are liquid at room temperature.
